This PR integrates [header pruning](https://github.com/celestiaorg/go-header/issues/260) into the node. The work of [dozens of PRs in go-header](https://github.com/celestiaorg/go-header/pulls?q=is%3Apr+sort%3Aupdated-desc++label%3Apruning+) finally lands with this PR.

## New
While this feature is quite broad, affecting most layers of the node's stack, for the user it is _mainly_ manifested with a few additions in the config (and significant reduction of disk usage consumption and synchronization/sampling speed)

```toml
  [Header.Syncer]
    # PruningWindow defines the duration within which headers are retained before being pruned.
    # Default is 337 hours.
    PruningWindow = "337h0m0s"
    # SyncFromHash is the hash of the header from which the syncer should start syncing.
    # Zero value to disable. Value updates up and down the chain are gracefully handled by Syncer.
    #
    # By default, Syncer maintains PruningWindow number of headers. SyncFromHash overrides this default,
    # allowing any user to specify a custom starting point.
    #
    # SyncFromHash has higher priority than SyncFromHeight.
    SyncFromHash = ""
    # SyncFromHeight is the height of the header from which the syncer should start syncing.
    # Zero value to disable. Value updates up and down the chain are gracefully handled by Syncer.
    #
    # By default, Syncer maintains PruningWindow number of headers. SyncFromHeight overrides this default,
    # allowing any user to specify a custom starting point.
    #
    # SyncFromHeight has lower priority than SyncFromHash.
    SyncFromHeight = 0
```

## Gotchas
Header pruning aims to be minimally breaking for the existing node runners. However, there are a few gotchas:

#### LNs no longer support historical queries
By default,  node maintains a sliding window of headers, bounded by Tail and Head headers. Requests with height below the Tail are rejected (This is, however, temporary, and lazy header fetching will be available with Backward Sync)

To retain the ability to request older queries with LNs, use new configuration fields to set an absolute header that the node will sync from, either the SyncFromHeight or the SyncFromHash field.

#### LNs only
Pruning for Bridge and Full nodes is disabled. Currently, the p2p protocol for headers cannot distinguish between pruned and non-pruned serving node types. Therefore, to keep *stable* synchronization of historical headers, we disable pruned servers.

#### Prolonged Starts 
* If your LN stores a significant portion of the history of headers, you may need to increase the `StartTimeout` value in the config, as LN prunes on start. If the starting times out, e.g., with the default 20s, the node will attempt to persist the progress, but storage state corruptions may still occur.  The complete mainnet header history pruning on moderate hardware takes under 100s, so update your config accordingly.
* If you move the tail down the chain (e.g., SyncByHeight 150 -> 100), you may need to increase the `StartTimeout` value in the config, as LN syncs the difference during start. (This is, however, temporary, and asynchronous syncing that doesn't block start will be available with Backward Sync).
  * __WARNING__: This feature wasn't tested extensively and may break in unknown ways. Use at your own risk!

#### Config Breaks
* `Daser.SampleFrom` field is no longer supported. Use `Header.Syncer.SyncFromHeight` instead.
* `Header.TrustedHash` field is no longer supported. Use `Header.Syncer.SyncFromHash` instead.

#### Replace
Replace for go-datastore was added, which may break users depending directly on the node's go.mod.
Do the following in your project's root to fix:
`go mod edit -replace github.com/ipfs/go-datastore=github.com/celestiaorg/go-datastore@48a63ae && go mod tidy`. It's gonna be removed in future releases.

## Manual Tests
- [x] Sync LN with a default config 
  - assert the tail is moving on every new head
  - assert it triggers block data pruning
  - assert Daser starts from Tail and syncs everything up to Head
  - assert storage usage stays relatively the same
- [x] Sync full header history by setting SyncFromHeight to 1
  - assert Daser and Pruner iterate over all headers, but skip most of them, respecting DPW
  - assert tail is absolute and constant
- [x] Update LN config to move the tail up (by changing window, height, or hash)
  - assert tail moves on Start and with reasonable speed
    - deleting headers 
    - triggering block data pruning
  - assert Daser doesn't break after the move
- [ ] Updated LN config to move the tail down (by changing window, height, or hash)
  - assert tail moves on Start by syncing missing headers

Some of the listed tests may become new or merged into an existing e2e test.

## TODO
 - [x] Disable header pruning for PFN. We decided to disable it as there is no way to distinguish between pruned and archival on the header exchange protocol. 
   - [x] Task in go-header to implement it
 - [x] Update windows to match recent CIPs
   - [x] TrustingPeriod (was missed in #4424)
   - Others will be done by https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/pull/4427
 - [x] Forbid DPW > HPW
 - [x] Recommend users to increase the start timeout
 - [ ] Docs in docs repo
 - [ ] E2e test covering some of the manual scenarios
 - [ ] Integration/functional test asserting interactions between the header store and pruner
 - [ ] Under the default settings where DPW == HPW, the data Pruner routine is always front-run by Syncer and only eats resources. Maybe think of a way to suspend it

perf(share/shrex): Improve shrex-eds sync by ~2.5x (#5207)

This PR speeds up EDS retrieval through shorter DAS work batches and a
larger peer pool. Shrex also prefers peers with higher verified
throughput and stops connection attempts quickly for unreachable peers.

⚠️ Each commit represents a single feature or fix, so this feature
branch is meant to be **merged** into main rather than squashed. ⚠️

### Results

**Control (v0.34.1)**: 28.23 blocks/s for 150,000 blocks (split into
archival ranges - early, mid, late); 3.76 MB/s is the aggregate across
three ranges of unequal size

**Feature branch (this PR)**: 63.52 blocks/s for the same 150,000
blocks; 8.46 MB/s

### Summary of changes
- 5239b292c
(https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/commit/5239b292ca1c6537cab95bf85ce65c5ed8f3b97b)
— Reduce the DAS sampling range and derive sample timeouts from square
size.

- 0862c4448
(https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/commit/0862c4448d857d1544712b4c3c7be41b8d2281c2)
— Scale the discovery peer limit with DAS concurrency.

- e00958194
(https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/commit/e009581940eee810307dfb67cd53d066ae2091b4)
— Add a five-second timeout for opening Shrex streams.

- c3f4d931d
(https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-node/commit/c3f4d931d4ea50c4e23cadf0414c9ba3158edf9c)
— Prefer peers with higher verified throughput through EWMA scoring.
